method: Rebuild from primary text, alongside can_lactation from which this clause takes the space requirements by cross-reference. Cal. Lab. Code §§1030-1034 were fetched from leginfo.legislature.ca.gov and read in full. The previous record for this clause was not a check at all: it said 'Implicated by the confirmed defect in can_lactation and checked against the evidence already recorded there; no new search.' Assertions describe the REBUILT body.
queries: Cal. Lab. Code §§1030-1034 full text, section by section (leginfo)
"Labor Code" "1030" OR "1031" lactation accommodation break time express milk employer

assertions.text: a reasonable amount of break time each time the employee needs to express milk
it runs concurrently with existing break time where possible, and non-concurrent break time is unpaid
assertions.note: §1030, final sentence. The previous body said 'and otherwise unpaid', which was right — this is the one thing the pair already had — but it did not tie the measure to the wage order's authorized rest time, which is what §1030 measures against.

assertions.text: break time is not required where it would seriously disrupt the employer's operations
a private space that is not a bathroom and meets the §1031 requirements
a written response is owed if break time or a compliant location cannot be provided
an employer with fewer than 50 employees may be excused from a requirement on showing undue hardship, and must still make reasonable efforts to provide a location other than a toilet stall
assertions.note: §1031(i). This was the defect the previous record identified and did not repair; it is now in the body, in the handbook's second-person voice.

assertions.text: denial of break time or adequate space is owed one additional hour of pay on the §226.7 basis
assertions.note: §1033(a). Note 'or adequate space' — the previous body said 'Denial of a required break', which is half the trigger.

assertions.text: the employee may complain to the Labor Commissioner, who may impose $100 per day
no discharge, discrimination or retaliation for exercising the right

priorDefects: omitted: §1031(i)'s undue-hardship exemption for employers with fewer than 50 employees. The previous record identified this and did not fix it; the clause shipped with the defect recorded in it.
omitted: denial of adequate SPACE as a trigger for the premium.
omitted: the $100-per-day civil penalty and the route to the Labor Commissioner.

method: the previous record was not an independent check. It says so: 'Implicated by the confirmed defect in can_lactation and checked against the evidence already recorded there; no new search.' A propagated verdict is not a verification, and the clause carried a verification level on the strength of one.
gaps: No decision construing §§1030-1034 was found on CourtListener, so 'seriously disrupt the operations of the employer' is stated to the employee with no gloss on what it means.

The premium is described by cross-reference to hb_meal_rest, which now carries Ferra's construction of the regular rate of compensation. If hb_meal_rest is edited without this clause being re-read, this clause will silently carry whatever it then says.
Whether the §226.7 premium and the §1033(c) penalty are both available for one denial was not researched.
§1031(f) and (g) — multiemployer worksites and agricultural employers — are not carried here or in can_lactation.
